hints: Remember that in an addition polymer, each C=C monomer becomes a two-carbon single-bonded unit in the chain, so work backwards in pairs.
Split the shown chain into alternating two-carbon pairs and count the Cl and CH3 groups on each pair.
Put the C=C double bond back between the two carbons of each different pair to rebuild the two original alkenes and name them.
walkthrough:
**Recall how addition polymers unzip**

Think of the long single-bonded chain as monomers that have opened their double bonds to join up. To find the monomers, we cut the chain back into two-carbon pieces.

Rule:
$$ \text{monomer } \text{C}=\text{C} \rightarrow \text{polymer } -\text{C}-\text{C}- $$

**Divide the section into two-carbon units**

Look from left to right. The chain alternates between two different patterns.

Pair type 1 (carbons 1-2, 5-6): $-\text{C}(\text{Cl})(\text{CH}_3)-\text{C}(\text{H})(\text{Cl})-$

Pair type 2 (carbons 3-4, 7-8): $-\text{C}(\text{Cl})(\text{CH}_3)-\text{C}(\text{H})(\text{CH}_3)-$

Notice each type has a different combination of $\text{Cl}$, $\text{CH}_3$ and $\text{H}$.

**Reform the double bonds to name the monomers**

Add the C=C back inside each pair.

Pair type 1 becomes $\text{C}(\text{Cl})(\text{CH}_3)=\text{C}(\text{H})(\text{Cl})$, which is $\text{CH}_3-\text{C}(\text{Cl})=\text{CH}(\text{Cl})$. This is a 3-carbon alkene with two Cl atoms on C1 and C2, called 1,2-dichloropropene.

Pair type 2 becomes $\text{C}(\text{Cl})(\text{CH}_3)=\text{C}(\text{H})(\text{CH}_3)$, which is $\text{CH}_3-\text{C}(\text{Cl})=\text{CH}-\text{CH}_3$. This is a 4-carbon alkene with one Cl on C2, called 2-chlorobut-2-ene.

**Conclude the copolymer pair**

The chain is an alternating copolymer of those two different units. That matches the combination of 1,2-dichloropropene and 2-chlorobut-2-ene.

options.A: Correct. The $-C(Cl)(CH3)-C(H)(Cl)-$ unit unzips to CH3-C(Cl)=CH(Cl), 1,2-dichloropropene, and the $-C(Cl)(CH3)-C(H)(CH3)-$ unit unzips to CH3-C(Cl)=CH-CH3, 2-chlorobut-2-ene. These two alternate along the chain shown.
options.B: Incorrect. 2,3-dichlorobut-2-ene would need a four-carbon unit with two Cl atoms, CH3-C(Cl)=C(Cl)-CH3, but no two-carbon pair in the diagram has that pattern. Chloropropene would have only one Cl, but one of the repeating pairs clearly has two Cl atoms.
options.C: Incorrect. Chloroethene is CH2=CHCl, a two-carbon monomer with no methyl group. Every two-carbon unit in the diagram carries at least one CH3 group, so a C2 monomer with no CH3 cannot be present.
options.D: Incorrect. Chloropropene has only one chlorine per molecule, for example CH2=C(Cl)-CH3. It cannot give the $-C(Cl)(CH3)-C(H)(Cl)-$ unit which needs two chlorines. That unit must come from a dichloro monomer.
